clue.text: Provide protective cover from tree line

definitions.meaning: to protect oneself against loss, as a financier does by offsetting a bet
a row of bushes or small trees marking a field boundary

explanation.surface: Someone shelters from the weather under a row of trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Investors offset risk this way, and a farmer plants a row of shrubs along a field edge; both senses share one word.

clue.text: From entrance, reversed opening

parts.note: a hatch is a small doorway or entrance, as on a ship
to back is to go in reverse, as a car does

explanation.surface: Someone backs out of a doorway they have just come through.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's rear door that swings upward is named after it, so the word denotes that kind of opening.

clue.text: Obtained little money from dispossessed

indicators.note: the small coin is taken away from the longer word, so 'from' signals the removal here

parts.note: the dispossessed are deprived of what they owned
P, a penny, is a small sum of British money

explanation.surface: Someone extracted a few coins from the destitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Something derived has been drawn or got from a source, a close synonym of obtained.

clue.text: Caught in front of endangered plane, do this?

definitions.text: Caught in front of endangered plane, do this?

indicators.note: front of tells us to take only the opening letter of the next word
the letter for caught is placed inside the letters that follow, so 'in' signals insertion

parts.note: a jet is a type of aeroplane
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A pilot trapped ahead of a plane in danger considers bailing out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as definition: a pilot of a plane in danger would use the ejector seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot leaves a doomed aircraft by firing out of the cockpit with the ejector seat, which is what the question suggests.

clue.text: Every year, the aristocracy must hold a great show

parts.note: PA is per annum, Latin for each year

indicators.note: the upper-class word has to keep the letter a within it, so 'must hold' signals containment

parts.note: the gentry are the landed upper class

explanation.surface: Each year the nobility stage a grand spectacle.
explanation.definitionFit: Pageantry is elaborate ceremonial display, a splendid public spectacle.

clue.text: Demonstrate about fine cause

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps around the other here

parts.note: to prove something is to demonstrate it
OK means fine or all right

explanation.surface: Protesters march over a penalty they have been charged.
explanation.definitionFit: To provoke something is to bring it about or give rise to it, so cause as a verb.

clue.text: 17, say, a miraculous relief?

definitions.meaning: the crime in 17 down is the killing of a deity, read as the end of a god
an unexpected piece of luck that seems sent from heaven

explanation.surface: A crime brings an unexpected blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 down is DEICIDE, the killing of a god, which can be read as GOD'S END.
explanation.definitionFit: A blessing arriving just when needed seems heaven-sent, and a deity's killing is literally a deity's finish.

clue.text: It's Borstal, as crook gets bird

indicators.note: crook as an adjective means bent or out of order, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A young offender from a reform school ends up serving time.
explanation.walkthrough: Borstal was a British reform institution for young offenders, and bird is slang for a prison sentence, which is the surface's misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: The albatross is a large ocean-going seabird with very long wings.

clue.text: Composter renewed section of earth

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A refreshed compost bin turns over a patch of garden soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrene is a literary adjective and noun for the land or the world as opposed to sea or sky.

clue.text: One creating ferment makes poet turn tail

indicators.note: the tail is the final pair of letters, and turning it swaps their order

parts.note: W B Yeats was the Irish poet

explanation.surface: A poet flees in fright.
explanation.definitionFit: This fungus makes dough rise and turns sugar to alcohol by fermentation.

clue.text: Informed about hard rocky ridge in several sections

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first word encloses the others

parts.note: told means informed
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a reef is a ridge of rock near the sea surface

explanation.surface: A geologist explains a hard ridge of rock made of layered sections.
explanation.definitionFit: Something threefold has three parts, which is a number of sections.

clue.text: Male has difficulty returning to a foreign country

indicators.note: returning means going back, so these letters are read from right to left

parts.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in Hamlet's 'there's the rub'

explanation.surface: A man struggles on his way back to a distant land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns M and RUB together, giving BURM, to which A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Burma, now officially Myanmar, is a country in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Proceed clumsily where one has no right to walk?

definitions.meaning: to move about awkwardly, like a poor dancer

definitions.text: where one has no right to walk?
definitions.meaning: a person whose both walking limbs are the left kind has none on the right side

explanation.surface: A trespasser blunders onto land where walking is forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no right' looks like a legal ban on walking, but it means no right foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone ungainly or bad at dancing, as if both feet were for one side.

clue.text: Scored rather slowly before judo expert intervenes

indicators.note: intervenes means comes between, so the expert's grade sits inside the other word

parts.note: ante is Latin for before
a dan is a black-belt grade in judo, hence an expert

explanation.surface: A judoka steps in before a slow-scoring sporting contest finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scored' points to sport, but it means written in a musical score.
explanation.definitionFit: This musical tempo marking means at a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: State of maid pecked in garden keeps one quiet

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the letter for one goes within the longer word

parts.words: State of maid pecked in garden
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Sing a Song of Sixpence a blackbird pecks off the nose of the maid hanging out clothes in the garden
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A garden maid attacked by a bird stays silent.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme's maid, hanging out the clothes, loses her nose to a blackbird, leaving her NOSELESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something noiseless makes no sound at all, a synonym of silent.

clue.text: See first part of Enigma code is broken

indicators.note: a broken code has its letters taken apart and put back together differently
first part of means only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Wartime codebreakers announce that a German cipher has been cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges E (from Enigma) with CODE and IS. 'See' is not a verb: it is a bishop's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is the area under that bishop's authority.

clue.text: Bound to have one's legs crossed

definitions.text: Bound to have one's legs crossed

parts.words: Bound to have one's legs crossed
parts.note: bound is a leap, not a certainty: a ballet jump in which the dancer beats the legs across each other in the air

explanation.surface: Someone is certain to sit with legs crossed.
explanation.definitionFit: This ballet step is a vertical leap in which the dancer crosses the feet rapidly in midair.

clue.text: Getting an increase as nanny? That's not serious

definitions.meaning: a nanny goat adds to the herd by giving birth to young
said of joking or teasing, as in 'you must be joking'

explanation.surface: A child-minder hears she is getting a pay rise and assumes it is a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nanny' suggests a child-minder, but it is a female goat; her young are kids.
explanation.definitionFit: A goat giving birth produces kids, and teasing or joking is the slang sense.

clue.text: Determine to limit one crime against humanity? No

indicators.note: to limit means to confine, so the word for determine encloses the letter for one

parts.note: to decide is to determine
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A court resolves to limit a single war crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The '? No' says it is a crime not against humanity but against a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing a god is an offence against divinity rather than against people.

clue.text: Showing more courage as one's boat capsizes on English river

indicators.note: a down clue's boat that capsizes turns upside down, so the letters read upward

parts.note: one's reads as I'S, I being one
a tug is a small boat that tows ships

explanation.surface: Someone braver than others watches their boat overturn on an English river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsizes' reverses the two pieces as one run, so the boat comes first, and 'on' places English and river after them, as in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Guts is slang for courage, so the comparative means braver.

clue.text: Shielded view of beast lifting a leg

definitions.text: Shielded view of beast lifting a leg

parts.words: Shielded view of beast lifting a leg
parts.note: a heraldic term for an animal shown on a coat of arms walking with one front foot raised

explanation.surface: A dog is seen through a screen raising its leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shielded' means shown on a heraldic shield, not screened.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry the term describes a beast walking with the right forepaw raised.

clue.text: People who are inquisitive about a first act of Parliament

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the nosy people enclose the letter a

parts.note: pryers are people who pry, nosy folk

explanation.surface: Nosy people ask about the first law passed by Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Each sitting of the UK Parliament opens with prayers, so 'act' is not a law here.
explanation.definitionFit: Sittings of both Houses at Westminster begin with devotions led by a chaplain, the opening business of the day.

clue.text: Create a cartoon creature with no tail, note

indicators.note: with no tail means the final letter is cut off the word for creature

parts.note: an animal is a creature
te is a note in tonic sol-fa, also spelt ti

explanation.surface: An animator draws a tailless beast and adds a note.
explanation.definitionFit: To make drawings move in a film is to bring a cartoon to life.

clue.text: Absolutely clear with hint weather's changing

indicators.note: changing means the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter

explanation.surface: A forecaster's hint that the weather is turning leaves the sky perfectly clear.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means morally spotless, completely beyond reproach, without stain.

clue.text: Delighted cry as TV doctor gets to work

parts.note: Doctor Who is the long-running BBC science-fiction series
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A television doctor sets to work with a cry of joy.
explanation.definitionFit: A whoop is a loud excited shout of joy.

clue.text: Old man at either end of 21, say

indicators.note: say means spoken, so the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: 21 across begins and ends with the same five-letter colour word

explanation.surface: An old man stands at each end of a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 across is WHITER THAN WHITE, which starts and ends with WHITE; 'Old man' is not the Isle's famous rock but an archaic word for a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Wight is an archaic word for a person or creature, now humorous.

clue.text: Fruit all dead?

parts.note: O as nought followed by live reads as none alive, which says that everyone is dead

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether all the fruit has died.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is the small oily fruit of a Mediterranean tree.

clue.text: Character I had to study in school endlessly

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

indicators.note: endlessly means both the first and the last letter are removed

parts.note: geography is a subject studied at school

explanation.surface: A pupil recalls having to study a subject forever.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideograph is a written symbol standing for an idea, as in Chinese script.

clue.text: Arguments about guaranteed amusements

indicators.note: about means around, so the legal arguments enclose the word for guaranteed

parts.note: pleas are arguments put forward in court
sure means certain or guaranteed

explanation.surface: Lawyers argue over assured entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasures are enjoyable diversions, things that give delight.

clue.text: Negotiate free gift

definitions.meaning: to discuss terms, as in to deal with an enemy
something paid for by someone else as a kindness

explanation.surface: A salesman bargains over a complimentary present.
explanation.definitionFit: Envoys may parley with rebels, and a friend's offer to pay for dinner is a kindness given at no cost.
